title: Fast-path OOM early-detection circuit breaker and micro-model hedging for graceful degradation
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Production serving nodes sometimes hit transient GPU memory pressure during heavy continuous-batching and long-sequence KV cache loads. Current mitigation relies on coarse eviction and model fallbacks which are either too slow (OOM occurs first) or too aggressive (degrades successful request throughput). This ticket implements a fast-path early-detection circuit breaker plus a micro-model hedging strategy to avoid hard OOMs while preserving latency and quality for most requests.

Scope:
- Add a lightweight fast-path OOM predictor in the admission path that runs a constant-time check on GPU reservation, aggregated batch headroom, and KV hotset estimate.
- Implement an early circuit-breaker that decides: (1) allow full path, (2) attempt aggressive KV compression/shrinking shim, (3) route to micro-model hedged replica (smaller quantized model), or (4) short-circuit with a graceful 503-like JSON response with retry hints.
- Hedge critical requests (high-priority tokens / authenticated enterprise tiers) to a low-latency micro-model simultaneously when admission risk is moderate; accept first completed response and cancel the other execution to reduce tail OOM exposure.
- Provide observability hooks: expose per-request decision path, predictor score, micro-model fallback used, and recovery latency. Integrate into Console rollout dashboard and SLO alerts.

Goals:
- Reduce hard OOM incidents by >= 80% on stressed nodes in canary clusters.
- Keep median P95 latency regression < 10% for standard tier and < 5% for enterprise-reserved paths.
- Maintain output quality: track embedding/token-level drift for hedged micro-models and enable per-customer rollout toggles.

Deliverables:
- Admission predictor module (C++ runtime + small Rust shim) with unit tests.
- Circuit-breaker state machine and config knobs (thresholds, backoff windows, per-customer overrides).
- Micro-model serving path: docker image plus validated quantized weights for hedged models, and graceful cancelation protocol.
- Console instrumentation + Grafana panels (predictor score distribution, fallback ratio, OOMs avoided).
- PR with load-test harness and canary rollout plan.

Out-of-scope: full KV compaction algorithms (handled by ENG-52310), long-term model-rolling strategy; those will be integrated later via dependencies.
acceptance_criteria: 1) In canary cluster, simulated continuous-batch stress runs show >=80% reduction in hard OOMs versus baseline within 2 hours. 2) Hedge path returns first-of-two responses; cancellation has <2% residual cost impact. 3) Console shows per-request decision_trace and metric emits: predictor_score, fallback_choice, canceled_executions. 4) Feature flag exists to toggle micro-model hedging per-customer.
implementation_notes:
Design notes and trade-offs: We purposely keep the predictor lightweight to avoid adding extra CPU/TX overhead. Predictor uses a moving-window reservoir estimate of KV hot page occupancy and a fast GPU free-memory read + per-batch reservation forecast. Thresholds are configurable: conservative for enterprise nodes, aggressive for best-effort.

Micro-model selection: Use an ordered ladder of pre-tested quantized variants (e.g., 8-bit int8, then int4/4k tokens) with documented quality regressions. Prefer model hedging over immediate eviction because hedging preserves user-perceived success rate.

Cancellation semantics: Support async cancellation tokens; aborted executions must return a small footprint release message so memory bookkeeping remains consistent.

Observability: Attach a compact decision_trace JSON string to request logs (max 1KB) and sample full traces for 1% of traffic for debugging.
progress_updates: 2026-03-02: Spike completed — implemented prototype predictor in test runtime; synthetic trace shows predictor score correlates with GPU mem pressure (Spearman 0.78).
2026-03-03: Design review with SRE and Console teams; requested realtime tracing key to integrate with rollout dashboard. Action: add decision_trace field and implement Prometheus counters.

2026-03-04: End-to-end test harness created (github.com/redwood/runtime/PR-2147). Load tests queued on canary cluster cluster-canary-7. Observed one hard OOM during initial run due to delayed cancelation; mitigation: introduce immediate free-token on cancel path.
review_feedback: PM (Lydia Chen): Ensure fallback quality monitoring — add regression alert if hedged outputs diverge beyond threshold per prompt set.
Design (Ravi Menon): UX for enterprise customers should include 'degraded mode' banner + retry guidance in the API response.
SRE (Hana Kim): Add burn-rate based backoff window to circuit-breaker to avoid oscillation under repeated pressure spikes.
next_steps: 1) Finish cancelation-safe memory-release implementation and run full canary. 2) Add per-customer feature flag and create Console toggle. 3) Run extended 48h soak; if results pass, prepare rollout playbook and postmortem template for incidents.
postmortem_plan: If rollout causes regressions, collect sampled decision_trace payloads (1% samples) and full heap dumps from canary nodes. Execute canary rollback and open incident ticket with timeline and mitigations.
notes_for_qa: QA should run matrix of sequences: short/medium/long sequences, varied batch sizes, with KV hotset manipulations. Validate cancellation idempotency and ensure canceled executions release GPU memory within 500ms.
customer_communication: Draft for status page and enterprise advisory created; step-by-step guidance for customers to opt out of hedging if they require strict model parity.
